grading.methodology: Complete ratings saved before grading-time plan/key disclosure; one assistant reviewer, partial blinding and no independent human validation

answer_quality.limitations: Small selected sample over six source PDFs; one assistant reviewer, partial blinding, AI-authored questions, no independent human validation. Mixed resource settings, days and cache states limit timing comparisons. Document-bootstrap intervals are descriptive; frozen retrieval decision unchanged.

generation.title: ML5.3 generation completion
generation.limitations: Different prompts, output lengths, priority, cache states and days; two administrative interruptions/retries; final seventy workers unloaded after every answer; user requested four threads, 85% RAM stop and 50% model CPU affinity ceiling after A038. No controlled speed comparison or guarantee against hardware faults.

decision.reason: At least one paired answer regressed; the predeclared screen does not permit adoption.

context_quality_train.limitations: Small AI-authored answerable TRAIN screen; single grader, only three document clusters. Bootstrap intervals are exploratory; no noninferiority or production-default claim. The assistant reviewer also prepared the source-linked questions; context lengths and study design were visible. No independent human or interrater validation. Citation-only errors affect grounding; wrong central claims affect correctness as well. A partial substantive answer with hedging is distinguished from an explicit refusal with an incorrect central claim.

context_revision_train.limitations: Development screen: six previously reviewed TRAIN cases plus four new assistant-authored probes (two answerable, two synthetic unsupported) over four TRAIN PDFs. Packing and prompting change together. Assistant review, partial blinding and shared authorship limit independence. Document-bootstrap intervals are exploratory with few clusters; no population, production latency or default-switch claim. Citation syntax checks do not prove semantic support. Cache/order and output length affect timing.

context_factorial_train.limitations: Diagnostic 2x2 study of ten previously reviewed, assistant-authored TRAIN cases over four PDFs, including two synthetic unsupported probes. No independent holdout or representative traffic. One fresh generation per condition/question, no generation seed, limited reviewer independence and partial blinding. Document-bootstrap intervals use few clusters and multiple exploratory contrasts without multiplicity correction. Counterbalanced order does not eliminate cache, carryover or output-length effects. No automatic live change or population claim.

context_refinement_train.limitations: Ten previously reviewed assistant-authored TRAIN cases over four PDFs, including two synthetic unsupported probes. One fresh generation per condition/question, no generation seed, partial blinding/shared authorship and prior familiarity. Four document clusters and multiple unadjusted document-bootstrap intervals make this exploratory. Reference retention is lexical, not semantic support. Order/cache/output lengths affect timing. No independent holdout, noninferiority, population or live-default claim.

context_coherence_train.limitations: Eighteen assistant-authored TRAIN cases over six PDFs: four previously reviewed sentinels, eight fresh answerable prompts and six synthetic unsupported probes. Fresh means new to this screen, not independent authorship or a holdout. One output per condition, partial blinding, shared authorship and six document clusters limit inference. Document-bootstrap intervals are exploratory. Quote retention is lexical; timing includes cache/order effects. No live-default or population claim.

next.reason: Complete the documentation using existing evidence; run ML6 only if explicitly chosen.

limitations: Six shared TEST PDF clusters; AI-authored questions; selected 50-case answer sample; one assistant reviewer with partial blinding and no independent human validation; unadjusted exploratory ablations; mixed resource settings and no end-to-end latency guarantee.
